A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSPG method and MFAX framework. All 26 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are available and readable; relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Linear Quadratic, Beach Bar, and Macroeconomics, library timing measurements in Table 2, and policy-representation ablations in Appendix C.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, timing measurements, and appendix ablations. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 gains an optional terminal-payoff initialization for the backward return, whereas v1 specifies zero initialization only. This is a limited correction to the stated procedure, consistent with the already-described terminal-reward environment. The recurrent policy, action parameterization, and blocking of gradients through mean-field transitions remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same partially observable Linear Quadratic, Beach Bar, and Macroeconomics environments. The new two-state counterexample in v2 Appendix A is a theoretical construction, not an additional experimental scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain SPG, IPPO, RIPPO, and M-OMD, with OpenSpiel and MFGLib retained in the library comparisons. v2 explains why AFP is excluded but does not evaluate it. Comparator membership in the retained figures and ablations is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 corrects Linear Quadratic's reported state count from 99 to 100 and its clipping boundary, removes a conflicting Beach Bar noise description, and adds principal wealth to consumption inside the Macroeconomics reward formula. These revise stated benchmark settings without establishing reruns. Evaluation metrics, hardware, budgets, and hyperparameter sweeps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The SPG/RSPG memory comparison, ordinal-versus-categorical policy ablation in Figure 11, and supplementary policy and population visualizations are retained. The added counterexample supplies theoretical evidence rather than a new empirical ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same uncertainty bands and reports 95% confidence intervals over 10 seeds in both versions. v2 shortens the caption but does not document additional runs, changed uncertainty estimation, or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds explicit qualitative capability entries: all three libraries support analytic mean-field updates, while only MFAX is marked as supporting sample-based updates. Benchmark outcomes are unchanged: Table 2 retains its timing values, and Figures 2–11 retain identical graphics, rankings, and behavioral findings.

T1.justification: v1 Section 5.1 justifies restricting private history using shared observations alone. v2 introduces Assumption 6.1, requiring the public history and current individual state to contain the relevant aggregate-state information. New Appendix A proves that this condition is not automatic: full-history policies can obtain reward 1 while restricted policies obtain only 1/2. This materially corrects the theoretical scope of the policy reduction.

C1.justification: The first history-aware HSM and MFAX contributions remain. However, v2 removes headline claims of state-of-the-art performance and first solving the partially observable macroeconomic game, emphasizing preservation of HSM convergence speed while learning history-dependent behavior.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies applicability: public-history sufficiency is presented as an additional assumption and an approximation in applications, with private-history omission potentially suboptimal. It also explicitly acknowledges missing convergence guarantees and explains why lower gradient variance need not produce lower across-seed performance variance. These materially sharpen the interpretation and limitations of the unchanged experiments.

D1.justification: v2 explains that one shared GRU embedding is computed per timestep and broadcast across states, defines the recurrent reset mask, and explicitly supplies the Macroeconomics AR(1) noise equation whose parameters were already listed. It also replaces the direct repository pointer with a project-page and usage-example pointer. Architecture sizes and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially broadens its positioning to numerical solvers, common-noise theory, deep learning, and cooperative mean-field control, adding works such as Achdou and Capuzzo-Dolcetta and Carmona and colleagues. It explicitly acknowledges that model-free RL can incorporate recurrence, sharpening RSPG's distinction around exploiting known structure. These changes exceed the accompanying publication-year and bibliography corrections.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Related Work moves before Preliminaries, the shared-observation argument is restructured around explicit assumptions, experimental subsections are consolidated, and Future Work becomes a separate section. Acknowledgements and revised author and affiliation text are also added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial relocation of figures and tables. Figure 1 moves near the introduction, Figures 2 and 3 share a page, equation boxes are added, and Table 1 gains two capability columns. All eleven underlying figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The decisive improvement is correction of an important logical overreach: v1 treats shared observations as sufficient to discard private histories, whereas v2 states an additional informational assumption and demonstrates strict suboptimality without it in Appendix A. This substantially improves scientific validity and claim calibration. Clearer implementation details also help reproducibility, although the retained experiments do not validate the new assumption or establish reruns following the environment-formula corrections.
